description:
The JMAP-ic0j.53 fix removed one leakage site at principal.rs:121 by replacing `JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string())` with `server_fail_from_backend(&e)`. That helper redacts to the constant `SERVER_FAIL_INTERNAL_DESC`. The closure note even cites "calendar.rs:68, event.rs:45-46, event.rs:105, event.rs:179-180, etc." as already using the helper.

But the helper is `fn server_fail_from_backend(&E) -> JmapError` — it only fits sites that produce a top-level `JmapError`. The handler-level `account_exists` / `get_state` / `get_objects` map sites use it correctly.

The /set per-id `notCreated`/`notUpdated`/`notDestroyed` map values are a DIFFERENT shape — they are `serde_json::Value` objects keyed by id, not `JmapError`. The helper does not fit. So every `BackendSetError::Other(e)` arm in every /set handler has the hand-rolled leaky pattern:

```rust
Err(BackendSetError::Other(e)) => {
    not_destroyed.insert(
        id_str,
        json!({ "type": "serverFail", "description": e.to_string() }),  // LEAK
    );
}
```

Sites in calendars-server (non-test paths):

- calendar.rs:150-153 (Calendar/set create BackendSetError::Other)
- calendar.rs:209-212 (Calendar/set update BackendSetError::Other)
- calendar.rs:267-272 (Calendar/set destroy — calendar_has_events transient `Err(e) → e.to_string()` site introduced by the bd:JMAP-ic0j.4 fix at bdf40aa)
- calendar.rs:301-303 (Calendar/set destroy — cleanup_calendar_events `Err(e) → description: e` where `e: String` was BUILT from backend Display via calendar.rs:408/419/451/463 inside the cleanup helper)
- calendar.rs:320-323 (Calendar/set destroy BackendSetError::Other)
- event.rs:297-300, 418-421, 463-466, 661-664, 721-724 (CalendarEvent/set + copy paths)
- event.rs:606 (CalendarEvent/copy serialize-source leak — separate site)
- event_notification.rs:138-141 (CalendarEventNotification/set destroy)
- participant_identity.rs:135-138, 190-193, 235-238 (ParticipantIdentity/set create/update/destroy)

Workspace-wide count (excluding worktrees and tests): roughly 100 sites across 7 extension-server crates — mail-server has the highest at ~30 sites (email.rs 7, mailbox.rs 6, sieve.rs 6, submission.rs 4, etc.), chat-server ~24 sites, contacts-server 8, filenode-server 9, tasks-server 9, metadata-server 6, sharing-server 4, calendars-server 12.

What callers cannot rely on:

- A backend author who carefully redacts secrets in `Self::Error::Display` (per the workspace JmapBackend::Error Display MUST-NOT contract tracked in JMAP-jfia.20) will see their redaction defeated for every /set per-id `Other` arm.
- The `description` field in /set error maps is part of the wire contract — clients parse it. Once a downstream user gets accustomed to seeing backend-flavored text there, redacting it to a constant becomes a behavioral-change SemVer-adjacent compatibility wart.
- A reader doing a security audit who searches for `e.to_string()` and `server_fail_from_backend` will find the principal.rs fix and assume the rest of the crate follows the same redaction discipline; they will be wrong.

What's needed:

A new helper at jmap-server level, parallel to `server_fail_from_backend`, that produces the per-id Value shape:

```rust
pub fn server_fail_value_from_backend<E: std::fmt::Display + ?Sized>(_err: &E) -> Value {
    json!({ "type": "serverFail", "description": SERVER_FAIL_INTERNAL_DESC })
}
```

…then a workspace-wide sweep across all 7 extension-server crates plus the cleanup_calendar_events helper signature (Result<(), String> → Result<(), BackendSetError<E>> or similar) so the typed error survives the helper boundary and the wire description is redacted at one chokepoint.

Per the workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" rule, the canonical jmap-mail-server change goes first, then propagates to every extension sibling in the same pass. This finding is filed under JMAP-ic0j (the calendars-server review epic) because the same anti-pattern is present in this crate's diff and the prior supplement at 18:11 missed the per-id Value-path scope; a workspace-wide standalone epic may be the actual landing pad.

Rusty pass #2 at 18:15 explicitly noted this finding was out-of-scope for /review-rusty and that "a workspace-wide bead for per-item BackendSetError::Other leakage might be worth filing under a different epic". This is that bead.
title: /set per-id 'serverFail' Value path bypasses redaction across calendar.rs:153/212/272/303/323, event.rs:300/421/466/606/664/724, event_notification.rs:141, participant_identity.rs:138/193/238 — same JMAP-ic0j.53 anti-pattern, workspace-wide
